title: I gave an AI four prompts and it made this pirate puzzle game, levels included, in my own AI C++ engine
author: MAuraEngine
selftext:
This is TREASURE!, a small Sokoban-style puzzle game made on MAura, a 3D engine I'm writing from scratch (using AI) in C++ (DirectX 12 / Vulkan, Jolt physics, games scripted in Lua).



The experiment: could an AI make a whole game on its own, with me giving almost no instructions? I wrote four prompts, roughly "make a grid puzzle, three levels, runs on any GPU, as beautiful and fun as possible", then "make it prettier in raster", then "localize it in English and Spanish". The AI chose the theme, the rules, the art and the effects.



The part I like most is the level design, because no one drew the levels:

\- A generator built random islands, millions of candidates for the first one.

\- A solver did an exhaustive search on each island, and only those where every crate, stone ball and powder keg is actually needed survived.

\- Among those, it kept the ones with the most dead ends for the player.

\- The shortest solution became the "captain's record" you try to match.

\- To check the game, an agent plays every solution inside the engine and fails the test if it doesn't reach the chest in exactly that many steps.



The mechanics: crates pushed into the sea float and make bridges, stone balls roll until they hit something and become stepping stones, and gunpowder kegs blow up the cracked rocks around the chest.



Graphics are raster only, so it runs on basically any card: simulated surf breaking on the shores, a different light for each island from morning to sunset, tilt-shift focus and wind in the palms. Art from Synty's POLYGON Pirate pack.



Happy to answer questions about the engine or the generator.

comments.author: Wide_Ship_9381
comments.body: What's the benefit of working on a custom engine rather than use Unity or Unreal at this point

replies.author: MAuraEngine
replies.body:
My engine was generated using AI. If you know how to prompt it, you can build anything.

It’s not about using a prompt like "make me the best 3D engine possible." You have to ask for things incrementally, check how the AI ​​handles them, and make corrections. You need to run tests and provide a lot of direction.

But once it’s built, you can modify it however you like to perfectly suit your needs.
